passage: In the staff room of the coaching centre, Mohit stared at the same line of the attendance sheet for a full minute. Sudha had joined as a trainer that Monday. Six years ago, in college, he had borrowed her lab file and lost it, then let the department believe she had been careless. She lost marks; he stayed silent. It still replayed at night. At tea break he said, "Sudha, can we talk? I lost your file in second year and never told you. I'm sorry. I know it cost you marks." She was quiet, then said, "I wondered." Mohit did not ask her to say it was fine. "If it helps, I can write to the department and set the record straight." She said she would think about it. Walking to the bus stop, he noticed the replay had gone quieter.

qa.q: What had Mohit done to Sudha's lab file six years ago?
qa.a: He borrowed her lab file and lost it, then let the department believe she had been careless.

qa.q: Why could Mohit not look away from the attendance sheet, and what was he feeling?
qa.a: Guilt over the lost file: it still replayed in his head at night, and seeing Sudha brought it back.

qa.q: What made Mohit's apology a sound one?
qa.a: He named what he did and what it cost her, did not ask to be told it was fine, and offered a way to repair it.

qa.q: How might Sudha see the apology after six years?
qa.a: Her reply of "I wondered" suggests she may have suspected all along and now feels acknowledged, though she wants time to decide about the offer.

grounding: A mistake from years ago still replays; Mohit owns the harm, apologises specifically, offers amends and then feels the guilt ease.

passage:
Rehana's diary. Friday.

It's been six years, and I still think about what I did to Irfan in college. I started a rumour that he'd cheated in the mid-term. I was jealous of his marks. It spread. People stopped sitting with him. He left the hostel mid-year.

I've replayed it hundreds of times. I've called myself every name.

Today, finally, I stopped just replaying it. I found Irfan online and wrote to him. I said exactly what I did, that it was a lie, that I was jealous, and that I was sorry for the months it cost him. I didn't ask him to forgive me. I offered to write to our old professor to clear his name, if he wanted.

He hasn't replied. He might never. That's his right.

But I'm going to stop punishing myself every night. I've owned it. I've tried to repair it. What I can do now is never do it to anyone again. That, I can promise.

qa.q: What rumour did Rehana start about Irfan?
qa.a: That he had cheated in the mid-term.

qa.q: What was Rehana feeling in the years after the rumour?
qa.a: Rehana felt deep guilt and shame, replaying it hundreds of times with harsh self-blame.

qa.q: What steps did Rehana take to repair the harm?
qa.a: Rehana wrote to Irfan admitting exactly what happened and why, apologised without asking for forgiveness, and offered to clear his name with their old professor.

qa.q: How might Irfan feel receiving Rehana's message?
qa.a: Irfan may feel a mix of old anger and some relief that the truth was finally admitted, and may need time before replying.

grounding: The diary shows someone still haunted by a harmful mistake from years ago, owning it, making amends where possible, and choosing to move on through changed behaviour.

Tenzin: that was 4 years ago and I still feel sick about it
Bhavna: that's a long time to carry it
Tenzin: I keep punishing myself. I can't even look at her photos online
Bhavna: have you thought about telling her?
Tenzin: I'm scared she'll hate me
Bhavna: she might be upset. but you'll have been honest. and you can offer to make it right
Tenzin: ok. I'll message her tonight. tell her exactly what happened
Bhavna: and then let yourself move on. you were 20. you're not that person
Tenzin: I'll also stop doing the silent thing. if I break something now, I say it immediately
Bhavna: that's the real repair

What was Tenzin feeling about the broken camera?

qa.q: What did Bhavna help Tenzin decide?
